clue.text: I am Bill and I make false claims

definitions.note: first-person riddle: the answer speaks about itself

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
a bill is a printed notice stuck up on a wall

explanation.surface: A man named Bill confesses to being a liar.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a name, but it is a poster; the definition speaks in the first person, as the answer would.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraud who pretends to be someone else is a person whose whole existence is a deceptive pretence.

clue.text: Intellectual lament broadcast

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A thinker's sorrowful complaint goes out on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe things belonging to the mind and its reasoning powers.

clue.text: Disturb peacekeepers on bench

parts.note: the United Nations sends peacekeeping forces
a settle is a high-backed wooden bench

explanation.surface: Someone disturbs soldiers in blue helmets sitting on a bench.
explanation.walkthrough: A settle is an old-fashioned wooden bench with arms and a high back.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle someone is to upset their calm, the same as disturbing them.

clue.text: Criticise "One Man and His Dog" on a point

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
M is a standard abbreviation for man or male
a pug is a small breed of dog
north is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone attacks the old BBC sheepdog-trial programme on a point of detail.
explanation.walkthrough: One Man and His Dog was a long-running British TV show about sheepdog trials; in a down clue 'on' puts the compass point after.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn a claim or a person is to challenge or attack it with criticism.

clue.text: Useless timber?

parts.note: surface reading: wood that is no good for anything
setter's reading: one word that in America means sawn wood and in Britain means useless junk

explanation.walkthrough: In British English the word also means old furniture and clutter cluttering a room, which is where 'useless' comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means sawn wood in American usage and unwanted bulky odds and ends in British usage, so both halves fit.

clue.text: Mountaineer lost his head but remained flexible

indicators.note: losing a head means the opening letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a mountaineer climbs

explanation.surface: A climber is beheaded but stays supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Limber is a synonym for supple, able to bend easily.

clue.text: Article Mail's reprinted on a living organism

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: something reprinted is set again, here with its letters arranged differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper article is reprinted, about some creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mail looks like the newspaper, but it is just four letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Any creature that lives, moves and feeds is an animal, a kind of living organism.

clue.text: Potential to reveal fresh talent

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the following word is made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A talent scout hopes new prospects will show their promise.
explanation.definitionFit: Latent means present but not yet developed, which is what potential describes as an adjective.

clue.text: Assembly of fifty Asters: security is the priority

indicators.note: an assembly puts parts together, so the letters are gathered into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener arranging fifty flowers puts security first.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a slogan saying that being safe comes before anything else, so security takes priority.

clue.text: Annoying youngster or model of significance?

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
taken as written
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: Asks whether a brat or a fashion model really matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' suggests a catwalk; in crosswords it often means T, from the Ford Model T.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter of great import is one of great significance or importance.

clue.text: Draw a parallel with prior notice; it's good enough

parts.note: an ad is a notice, and 'prior' puts it first
to equate is to treat two things as alike

explanation.surface: Comparing with an earlier warning shows it suffices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior' is the positional signal: the advertisement comes before the comparing verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adequate is satisfactory or sufficient, meeting the need without excelling.

clue.text: Some on-board entertainment creates an impression

indicators.note: some means only a part of the following words is taken

parts.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: In-flight films leave a mark on the passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A dent is a hollow pressed into a surface, a physical impression.

clue.text: In place of "occupier" see "officer"

parts.note: 'in lieu of' means in place of
a tenant occupies a rented property

explanation.surface: Reads like a dictionary instruction swapping one word for another.
explanation.walkthrough: The rank itself comes from French for 'place-holder', one acting in place of a superior.
explanation.definitionFit: A lieutenant is a commissioned rank in the army or navy, hence an officer.

clue.text: Attractive girl has a lot of money

parts.note: pretty means good-looking
Penny is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A good-looking young woman is rich.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'cost a pretty penny' means a large sum of money.

clue.text: Cot and chair arranged about the chest

indicators.note: furniture that is arranged is set out in a new order, as these letters are

parts.note: the two pieces of furniture, 'and' joining them

explanation.surface: Bedroom furniture is set out round a chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: The chest looks like furniture beside the cot and chair, but it is the body's ribcage.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoracic describes anything relating to the thorax, the part of the body between neck and abdomen.

clue.text: Short film showing modern southern dance

parts.note: modern means new
S abbreviates southern
a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: A short documentary features a new dance from the South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reel' is also film, which makes the surface neat but is not the definition here.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsreel was a short cinema film of current events shown before the main feature.

clue.text: Info on one American's wizardry

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
the Roman numeral for one
US abbreviates American

explanation.surface: Gossip about one American's magic skill.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for the facts or the lowdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Genius is exceptional brilliance, which is what wizardry means figuratively.

clue.text: Brutal attack

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to maul or criticise fiercely

explanation.surface: A vicious assault.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adjective for ferocious and as a verb for mauling, as a dog might a person.

clue.text: Organic process demolished mobile mast

indicators.note: a demolished structure is broken up, so the letters are knocked down and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A phone mast is pulled down in an organic, natural way.
explanation.definitionFit: Metabolism is the set of chemical processes that keep a living body going.

clue.text: Way to get to a place for an event

parts.note: taken as written
a venue is where an event is held

explanation.surface: Directions for reaching an event's location.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a broad road, and Way is also a name for a road.

clue.text: A thousand agree, perhaps: it's skimpy

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: perhaps hints the word could take another form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A thousand people may agree that something is too small.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means lacking in quantity, which is what skimpy describes.

clue.text: Seven days sound pathetic

indicators.note: sound means we go by how the words are said, not how they are spelt

parts.note: seven days make a week

explanation.surface: Someone says a week's effort was poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning solid, the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Weak in the sense of feeble or unconvincing is a synonym of pathetic.

clue.text: Go indirectly by perimeter roads

parts.note: a side is an edge, part of the perimeter
ways are roads

explanation.surface: A driver takes the ring roads to avoid the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Going sideways means moving obliquely, not straight ahead, so not directly.

clue.text: Marina arranged to produce flier

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, as these letters are

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman named Marina organises a leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' looks like a printed leaflet; it is someone who flies.
explanation.definitionFit: An airman is a pilot or member of an air force, someone who flies.

clue.text: Boss's one love is his workplace

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud
the Roman numeral for one
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: The boss's one true love is his office.
explanation.walkthrough: Boss looks like an employer, but here it is a decorative knob, a stud.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is the room where an artist, photographer or broadcaster works.

clue.text: Get wind of a piece of cake

explanation.surface: Someone finds out about a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get wind of' reads as one idiom meaning hear about; split it, and the middle word is the first definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a gentle wind and, informally, a task that is effortless.
